`./compile.sh` reports **"compiled OK"** on the first attempt — no errors, only a benign deprecation note (expected, since I test the library's own deprecated `withXxx` methods).

Summary of what was built: `tests/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVFormatAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class (package `org.apache.commons.csv`) covering `CSVFormat`'s documented contract from `api/`:

- All 12 predefined format constants (`DEFAULT`, `EXCEL`, `MYSQL`, `ORACLE`, etc.) against their documented builder settings
- `CSVFormat.Predefined` enum (`getFormat()`, `values()`, `valueOf`, null/invalid-name errors)
- `newFormat(char)` defaults and line-break rejection
- `Builder`: defaults, `create(CSVFormat)`, fluent chaining, `Supplier<CSVFormat>` contract, every documented setter round-tripped through its getter, defensive copying of header/header-comment arrays, validation errors (line-break chars for escape/comment marker)
- `equals`/`hashCode` contract, including `HashSet` bucket behavior
- Package-private helpers accessible from the same package: `copy()`, `copy(CSVFormat)`, `clone(T...)`, `getEscapeChar()`, `getDelimiterCharArray()`
- `format(Object...)` quoting/escaping/null-substitution/multi-char-delimiter behavior
- `print(Object,Appendable,boolean)`, `printRecord`, `println`, `print(Appendable/File/Path, Charset)`, `printer()` (via `System.out` capture)
- `parse(Reader)` using the package-summary's documented iteration idiom, plus header-skip, `maxRows`, and empty-line handling interactions
- Deprecated `withXxx` methods and `getDelimiter()`/`getAllowDuplicateHeaderNames()`
- `Serializable` round-trip

No tests were executed, per the restrictions — only compiled.
